newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Opposition may protest Singapore election result.
newsitem.headline: Opposition may protest Singapore election result.

text.p: Singapore's opposition Worker's Party (WP) said on Friday it might protest against the result in a hotly-contested seat in elections it charged would go down as a "very dirty chapter" of the country's history.
Party leader Joshua Jeyaretnam told a news conference Thursday's elections, in which opposition parties won just two of 83 seats in parliament, were a "setback" to the development of democracy.

He said his left-party would consider whether to lodge an official protest at the result in the Cheng San multi-member constituency, where the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) won with 55 percent of the vote.
The PAP had won the election before a vote was cast after the opposition contested only 36 seats.

Nevertheless, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong ran a no-holds-barred campaign and focused all the PAP's heavy weapons on the multi-member constituency of Cheng San, where Jeyaratnam led the Workers' Party team in a winner-takes-all contest.

Goh alleged that Tang Liang Hong, a member of the five-man Workers' Party team, was a "Chinese chauvinist" who endangered Singapore's multi-ethnic harmony. Goh and Tang are suing each other over remarks made during the bitter contest.
"The contested election of this general election registered a very dirty chapter of Singapore's political history," Tang told the news conference.
Jeyaretnam was also angry. "This is the first time that the threats are so naked. Singapore suffered a setback on the road to establishing a democracy," he said.
"It is a mockery to say the elections were fair and free," he said.
Jeyaretnam also accused the PAP of violating election laws and said action should be taken against offenders.
But he declined to confirm whether he would petition the government to have the Cheng San results declared void.
"The party will have to consider it," he said, when asked if the WP would act on its perceived complaints. He said appeals could also be made to the United Nations electoral commission.
Jeyaretnam cited three legal provisions he alleged might have been violated during the Cheng San battle.
These included the presence of Goh and two deputy prime ministers at polling centres and their meeting and talking to voters before they cast their ballots.

"Mid-way through the morning, there were long queues of voters from the steps of the voting (centre) to the gate and (Deputy Prime Minister) Lee Hsien Loong inspected this parade that had been drawn out for him. He went along shaking hands with every one of them," Jeyaretnam said.
"I was told of this. I confirmed this with the sergeant (of police). I lodged a strong protest with the ARO (assistant returning officer) and informed the police about it."
"If it is (a violation of election law)...action should be taken after we lodge our report against these worthy gentleman."
Jeyaretnam also blasted Singapore media he accused of propagating PAP views.
"The biggest tragedy in Singapore (is) we believe we have a press speaking for the people but it isn't. It only speaks for the government," he said.
